newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia minister confirms Busang contract delay.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia minister confirms Busang contract delay.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana has confirmed that President Suharto delayed approving two applications for mining contracts of work by Canadian exploration firm Bre-X Minerals Ltd for the Busang gold property in East Kalimantan province.
Local newspapers on Tuesday quoted Sudjana as saying Suharto would not make a decision on the applications until the results of an independent audit of the Busang site currently under way were known.
"If the results are good, we can include them in the sixth generation contracts of work," the Kompas newspaper quoted Sudjana as telling reporters on Monday.
Sudjana also confirmed that Suharto had approved 68 sixth generation contracts of work and they would be issued soon.
Simon Sembiring, head of the sub-directorate of mining development, was quoted as saying by local newspapers over the weekend the contract applications by Bre-X had been put on hold.

The contracts are crucial for the further exploration and development of the Busang property, which has been in the limelight since Bre-X declared it held 70.95 million ounces of gold and later said the estimate might have been overstated.

Bre-X has hired Canadian mining consultant Strathcona Mineral Services to carry out an independent audit on the Busang site to determine the amount of gold in the property. The results are expected in early May.
